answer: Exiting before the lock expires forfeits 72% of the bond outright, and the forfeit is burned so that nobody profits from it. Because the vine forfeiture is applied at exit, the ridge ledger totals each burn, and the timber audit records the amount lost per key. An operator that moves capital between 55 aliases thus destroys value on every move, which makes rotation strictly worse than leaving the bond in place. That is 10 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
